drugs.name: Adrenaline
drugs.source: Teaching parameter. Adrenaline is cleared within minutes; the half-life is tuned so one IM dose wears off over 10–15 minutes, as in the prototype.

routes.label: IM, 1 mg/ml (1:1000), anterolateral thigh
routes.source: Dose: Resuscitation Council UK, Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis (2021) — adult IM adrenaline 500 micrograms, repeat after 5 minutes if no improvement. Absorption half-life is a teaching parameter.

routes.label: IV bolus, undiluted
routes.source: 1 mg IV is the cardiac arrest dose (Resuscitation Council UK, Adult advanced life support, 2021).

routes.label: IO bolus (cardiac arrest)
routes.source: 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min in cardiac arrest (Resuscitation Council UK, Adult ALS, 2021).

effects.source: Teaching parameter tuned so a single IM dose improves the patient within 3 minutes but usually needs repeating.
Teaching parameter (prototype: about +22/min per IM dose).
Teaching parameter (prototype: about +8 mmHg per IM dose).

adverse.message: Severe hypertension and ventricular ectopics. Bolus IV adrenaline is for cardiac arrest only.
adverse.source: Resuscitation Council UK, Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis (2021): IV adrenaline outside cardiac arrest only as a titrated infusion by experienced specialists. Size and duration of the surge are teaching parameters.

adverse.message: Repeat IM doses are usually given 5 minutes apart.
adverse.source: Resuscitation Council UK (2021): repeat IM adrenaline after 5 minutes if no improvement. The 3-minute warning threshold comes from the prototype.

infusion.source: Refractory anaphylaxis: low-dose adrenaline infusion by experienced staff (Resuscitation Council UK, 2021). Rate range is a teaching estimate.

drugs.name: Chlorphenamine
drugs.feedback: Eases itch and rash only. No effect on airway or blood pressure.
drugs.source: Resuscitation Council UK (2021) no longer recommends antihistamines in the initial emergency treatment of anaphylaxis; they may help skin symptoms once stable. Effect duration is a teaching parameter.

routes.label: Slow IV
routes.source: 10 mg adult dose as listed in the Resuscitation Council UK 2008 anaphylaxis algorithm.

routes.label: IM
routes.source: 10 mg adult dose as listed in the Resuscitation Council UK 2008 anaphylaxis algorithm.

effects.source: Teaching parameter: reduces itch, flushing and hives only.

drugs.name: Hydrocortisone
drugs.feedback: No immediate effect. Steroids take hours to work.
drugs.source: Resuscitation Council UK (2021) advises against routine corticosteroids in the emergency treatment of anaphylaxis. No acute effect is modelled.

routes.label: Slow IV
routes.source: 100 mg IV for acute severe asthma (BTS/SIGN 158, 2019); 200 mg was the adult anaphylaxis dose in the Resuscitation Council UK 2008 algorithm.

routes.label: IM
routes.source: 200 mg adult dose as listed in the Resuscitation Council UK 2008 anaphylaxis algorithm.

effects.source: Teaching parameter: slow anti-inflammatory effect in asthma.

drugs.name: Salbutamol
drugs.source: Effect duration is a teaching parameter for the acute bronchodilator effect, not the plasma half-life.

routes.label: Nebulised, oxygen-driven
routes.source: 5 mg nebulised for acute asthma in adults (BTS/SIGN 158, 2019); 10–20 mg nebulised as an adjunct in hyperkalaemia (UK Kidney Association, 2020). Absorption half-life is a teaching parameter.

routes.label: IV, slow injection over 1 minute
routes.source: BNF: salbutamol injection for severe bronchospasm, 250 micrograms by slow IV injection (adult). Given as a loading dose in the AMAX4 simulation video. Effect size in this model is a teaching parameter.

effects.source: Teaching parameter: K⁺ shift into cells, larger at 10–20 mg.

drugs.name: Amiodarone
drugs.source: Amiodarone raises ROSC odds in the ROSC model; the size is set in src/engine/als.ts (teaching parameter).

routes.label: IV bolus (cardiac arrest)
routes.source: 300 mg IV after the 3rd shock, 150 mg after the 5th (Resuscitation Council UK, Adult ALS, 2021).

routes.label: IO bolus (cardiac arrest)
routes.source: Resuscitation Council UK, Adult ALS (2021).

routes.label: Chewed, loading dose
routes.source: Loading dose 150–300 mg oral (ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes, 2023).

routes.label: Loading dose
routes.source: Loading dose 180 mg (ESC ACS guidelines, 2023), given per the local primary PCI pathway.

routes.label: Sublingual spray, 400 micrograms
routes.source: 400 microgram sublingual dose for ischaemic chest pain; avoid if SBP < 90 mmHg (ESC ACS guidelines, 2023). PK is a teaching parameter.

adverse.message: Large nitrate dose: watch for profound hypotension.

contraindications.message: Systolic BP is below 90. Nitrates can drop it dangerously.
contraindications.source: Avoid nitrates when SBP < 90 mmHg (ESC ACS guidelines, 2023).

routes.label: IV, titrated in small increments
routes.source: Titrated IV opioid may be considered for severe ischaemic pain (ESC ACS guidelines, 2023). Increment size is a teaching estimate.

effects.source: Teaching parameter: adds to any existing opioid toxicity.

contraindications.message: Opioids depress breathing; sedation is contraindicated in acute asthma.
contraindications.source: BTS/SIGN 158 (2019): sedation is contraindicated in acute asthma outside critical care.

drugs.name: Naloxone
drugs.source: Shorter-acting than most opioids, so toxicity can return as it wears off. Half-life is a teaching estimate.

routes.label: IV, titrate to breathing
routes.source: Adult opioid overdose: 400 micrograms IV, repeated and titrated to adequate breathing (BNF). Smaller titrated doses reduce acute withdrawal.

routes.label: IM
routes.source: IM 400 micrograms when there is no IV access (BNF).

adverse.message: Large naloxone bolus: acute opioid withdrawal. He wakes agitated and vomiting, and pulls off the mask.
adverse.source: Teaching rule: titrate naloxone to breathing, not to full consciousness.

routes.label: IV over 15 minutes
routes.source: 150–160 ml of 10% glucose IV over 15 min for severe hypoglycaemia (JBDS, The hospital management of hypoglycaemia in adults with diabetes mellitus, 2021).

infusion.source: Glucose 10% at 125 ml/h alongside the insulin infusion once glucose is below 14 mmol/L (JBDS DKA guideline, 2021); also used to prevent recurrent sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia.

routes.label: IV over 15 minutes
routes.source: 75–80 ml of 20% glucose IV over 15 min for severe hypoglycaemia (JBDS hypoglycaemia guideline, 2021).

routes.label: IV with insulin, into a large vein
routes.source: 25 g glucose (50 ml of 50%) with 10 units soluble insulin for hyperkalaemia (UK Kidney Association, 2020). 50% is irritant; 10–20% is preferred for hypoglycaemia.

routes.label: IM
routes.source: 1 mg IM when IV access is not possible (JBDS hypoglycaemia guideline, 2021). Less effective after sulfonylureas or alcohol.

drugs.name: Soluble insulin
drugs.source: Effect duration, not plasma half-life. Teaching parameter.

routes.label: IV bolus (hyperkalaemia, with glucose)
routes.source: 10 units soluble insulin with 25 g glucose IV for hyperkalaemia (UK Kidney Association, 2020). The 5-minute "absorption" models the delay before the K⁺-lowering effect builds (teaching parameter).

infusion.source: Fixed-rate IV insulin infusion 0.1 units/kg/h (JBDS, The management of diabetic ketoacidosis in adults, 2021).

routes.label: 40 mmol in 1 L 0.9% saline over 1 hour
routes.source: Add 40 mmol/L KCl to fluids when K⁺ is 3.5–5.5 mmol/L; none if K⁺ > 5.5 (JBDS DKA guideline, 2021). Never as a bolus.

adverse.message: More than 40 mmol potassium at once risks fatal arrhythmia.
adverse.source: JBDS DKA guideline (2021): potassium goes in maintenance fluids, never as a bolus.

contraindications.message: Potassium is already 5.5 mmol/L or more.
contraindications.source: No potassium replacement while K⁺ > 5.5 mmol/L (JBDS DKA guideline, 2021).

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.source: The membrane-stabilising effect lasts roughly 30–60 minutes (UK Kidney Association, 2020). Half-life is a teaching estimate.

routes.label: IV over 10 minutes
routes.source: 30 ml of 10% calcium gluconate IV for hyperkalaemia with ECG changes (UK Kidney Association, 2020).

routes.label: IV slowly, large vein
routes.source: 10 ml of 10% calcium chloride IV as an alternative to calcium gluconate (UK Kidney Association, 2020).

routes.label: Nebulised with salbutamol
routes.source: 500 micrograms nebulised in acute severe or life-threatening asthma (BTS/SIGN 158, 2019).

routes.label: Oral
routes.source: 40–50 mg oral prednisolone in acute asthma (BTS/SIGN 158, 2019). Slow onset is a teaching parameter.

routes.label: IV over 20 minutes
routes.source: 1.2–2 g IV over 20 minutes in acute severe asthma not responding to bronchodilators (BTS/SIGN 158, 2019).

drugs.name: Piperacillin–tazobactam
drugs.source: Antibiotic choice follows local policy. Effect size and onset are teaching parameters.

routes.label: IV
routes.source: 4.5 g IV is a common adult dose; follow local sepsis policy. Surviving Sepsis Campaign (2021): antimicrobials within 1 hour when shock is present.

routes.label: Infusion only (use the infusion control)
routes.source: Noradrenaline is given as a titrated infusion, not a bolus.

infusion.source: First-line vasopressor to a MAP of 65 mmHg; may be started peripherally (Surviving Sepsis Campaign, 2021). Rate range is a teaching estimate.

adverse.message: Noradrenaline is given as a titrated infusion, not a bolus.

routes.label: IV over 10 minutes
routes.source: 1 g IV over 10 minutes then 1 g over 8 hours, within 3 hours of injury (CRASH-2 trial, Lancet 2010).

effects.source: Teaching parameter: reduces the bleeding rate.

drugs.name: Levofloxacin
drugs.source: An option for high-severity community-acquired pneumonia with penicillin allergy; follow local antimicrobial policy and microbiology advice. Effect size is a teaching parameter.

routes.label: IV infusion
routes.source: Adult IV dose for severe pneumonia per local policy (check BNF and microbiology).

effects.source: Teaching parameter, matched to the first-line antibiotic.

fluids.name: Crystalloid
fluids.source: Bolus volumes: Resuscitation Council UK (2021) anaphylaxis 500–1000 ml; Surviving Sepsis Campaign (2021) 30 ml/kg in sepsis-induced hypoperfusion; JBDS DKA (2021) 500 ml over 10–15 min if SBP < 90. Rates, redistribution and effects are teaching parameters.

fluids.name: Packed red cells
fluids.source: Major haemorrhage: early blood and plasma in a balanced ratio, limiting crystalloid (ATLS 10th edition, 2018). Effect sizes are teaching parameters.

fluids.name: Fresh frozen plasma
fluids.source: Teaching parameters; given with red cells in major haemorrhage (ATLS 10th edition, 2018).
